title: HAIL-DIMM: Host Access Interleaved with Near-Data Processing on DIMM-based Memory System
problem: Near-data processing can interfere with host memory access, compromising system fairness. A cost-effective LRDIMM-based NDP solution is needed that seamlessly interleaves NDP with host requests without dedicated memory resources.
motivation: Reducing data movement between host and memory is critical for improving performance and energy efficiency in modern computing systems.
method: HAIL-DIMM disguises NDP operations (which combine data movement with computation happening at the memory) as standard DDR READ/WRITE commands so the memory controller sees them as regular requests. The controller's built-in interleaving logic (which spreads requests across memory banks to balance load) naturally schedules them fairly with host access, without needing dedicated hardware. Meanwhile, the DIMM recognizes which commands are NDP work based on their address and executes them as computation. This dual interpretation—same request looks like DDR to the controller but NDP to the DIMM—enables fair interleaving using only existing system hardware.
key_novelty: HAIL-DIMM's key innovation is using the same request format for two different purposes: the memory controller reads it as a standard DDR operation while the DIMM interprets it as near-data processing (computation happening at the memory), enabling fair interleaving without extra hardware.
contributions: LRDIMM-based NDP architecture that ensures fairness without interfering with host access
Address-based mechanism for dual-level request interpretation leveraging bank interleaving
FPGA prototype demonstrating production viability and proof-of-concept
Achieves 2.19x latency speedup and 45.4% energy savings for memory-bound workloads
limitations: Scalability to larger systems and applicability beyond memory-bound workloads not discussed.
